claims.text: Adding 3–5 at.% Ag to as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type HEAs promotes more uniform chemical and microstructural ordering.
Ag-mediated ordering makes magnetic exchange interactions more homogeneous and reduces fluctuations in exchange energies.
Ag plays primarily a structural role because it is an FCC metal additive.
More homogeneous exchange interactions broaden the magnetostructural transition.
More homogeneous exchange interactions reduce hysteretic losses during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Ag addition mitigates phase separation or abrupt structural changes during the magnetostructural transition.
Mitigating phase separation or abrupt structural changes produces a smoother magnetocaloric transition.
The Ag-alloyed material will retain a significant magnetocaloric response under low applied fields.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type baseline is a single-phase hexagonal material.
The as-deposited baseline undergoes a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
The baseline transition produces a large, hysteretic magnetic entropy change.
The as-deposited baseline has limited heat-exchange capability because of a low surface-to-volume ratio.
Retaining the overall non-equiatomic balance while adding Ag will maintain mechanical stability and cost-effectiveness.
The predicted Ag effect should apply to similarly processed FeMnNiGeSi-type films or rapidly cooled materials near their transition temperature.
Extreme composition changes or processing routes that alter phase stability may fall outside the prediction's domain.

contradictions.description: The proposed mediator narrows the distribution of exchange energies by increasing homogeneity, yet the predicted result is a broader temperature-dependent transition. Without an additional source of broadening, reduced interaction variability would more naturally suggest a narrower transition, so these parts of the mechanism are in tension.
